summary.en: A Khmer port called Prey Nokor, settled by Vietnamese in the 17th century and organised as Gia Định in 1698. As Saigon it was the capital of French Cochinchina and of South Vietnam, and was renamed after Hồ Chí Minh in 1976.
summary.zh: 原为高棉港口波雷诺哥，17世纪越南移民迁入，1698年设嘉定府。以西贡之名先后作为法属交趾支那和南越的首府，1976年以胡志明之名命名。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ho Chi Minh City
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: Ho Chi Minh City

note: The start of Vietnamese settlement and the date of the Khmer name are approximate.

polity.zh: 唐安南都护府 / 地方自主政权
阮朝 / 法属印度支那

summary.en: On the Red River, the Tang citadel of Đại La became Thăng Long when the Lý made it their capital in 1010. Renamed Hà Nội in 1831, it was the capital of French Indochina and has been Vietnam's capital since 1945.
summary.zh: 红河畔的唐代大罗城于1010年被李朝定为都城，改名升龙。1831年改称河内，曾为法属印度支那首府，1945年起为越南首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Hanoi
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Central Sector of the Imperial Citadel of Thang Long – Hanoi
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Hanoi

note: Hanoi was also capital of French Indochina from 1902.

polity.zh: 荷兰东印度公司 / 荷属东印度

summary.en: The pepper port of Sunda Kelapa was taken by Fatahillah in 1527 and renamed Jayakarta. The Dutch rebuilt it as Batavia in 1619; renamed Jakarta during the Japanese occupation, it became the capital of independent Indonesia.
summary.zh: 胡椒港口巽他格拉巴于1527年被法塔希拉攻占并改名查雅加达。1619年荷兰人在此重建巴达维亚；日本占领期间改称雅加达，后成为独立的印度尼西亚首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Jakarta
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Jakarta

note: The start of Sunda Kelapa as a port is approximate; Wikidata dates the city's founding to 22 June 1527.

polity.zh: 孟族王国 / 东吁王朝

summary.en: A Mon town around the Shwedagon Pagoda, Dagon was renamed Yangon ("end of strife") by Alaungpaya in 1755. Under British rule Rangoon became the capital of Burma, which it remained until the government moved to Naypyidaw in 2005.
summary.zh: 大光原为瑞德宫大金塔周围的孟族城镇，1755年雍籍牙将其改名仰光（意为“战争终结”）。英国统治时期仰光成为缅甸首府，直至2005年政府迁往内比都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Yangon
G. E. Harvey, History of Burma (Longmans, 1925)
Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, Vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
Wikipedia: Yangon

note: Wikidata's founding date of 1035 is traditional; 1000 is used as an approximate start.

summary.en: A riverside customs and fort town on the Chao Phraya under Ayutthaya, it became the capital when Taksin settled at Thonburi in 1767 and Rama I founded the new royal city on the east bank in 1782.
summary.zh: 阿瑜陀耶时期湄南河畔的关卡与要塞小镇。1767年郑信定都吞武里，1782年拉玛一世在东岸建立新王城，曼谷由此成为都城。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Bangkok
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
David K. Wyatt, Thailand: A Short History (Yale University Press, 2nd ed. 2003)
Wikipedia: Bangkok

note: The date of the early settlement is approximate.

polity.zh: 菲律宾（法定首都为奎松城）

summary.en: A fortified Muslim trading settlement on Manila Bay, Maynila was taken by Legazpi, who founded the Spanish city in 1571. It was the hub of the trans-Pacific galleon trade and has been the Philippine capital except in 1948–1976, when Quezon City held the title.
summary.zh: 马尼拉湾畔设防的穆斯林贸易聚落，被黎牙实比攻取后于1571年建立西班牙城市。这里是跨太平洋大帆船贸易的枢纽，除1948—1976年奎松城为法定首都外，一直是菲律宾首都。

sources.title: Emma H. Blair & James A. Robertson (eds.), The Philippine Islands, 1493–1898, Vol. 3 (1903)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Manila
Philippine News Agency/PTV: How QC became biggest LGU in Metro Manila (RA 333 of 1948; PD 940 of 1976)

note: The pre-Hispanic polity's origins are not precisely dated. Republic Act 333 (1948) made Quezon City the capital; Presidential Decree 940 (1976) restored Manila.

polity.zh: 马来亚联合邦；1963年起为马来西亚

summary.en: Founded by Parameswara around 1400, Malacca controlled the strait that bears its name and was the region's richest port. It passed to the Portuguese (1511), Dutch (1641) and British (1824), leaving a layered colonial townscape.
summary.zh: 马六甲约于1400年由拜里米苏拉建立，控制着以其命名的海峡，是区域最富庶的港口。此后相继归属葡萄牙（1511年）、荷兰（1641年）与英国（1824年），留下层叠的殖民城市风貌。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Melaka and George Town, Historic Cities of the Straits of Malacca
Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Wikipedia: Malacca City

note: British occupation 1795–1818 during the Napoleonic Wars is merged into the Dutch period.

summary.en: Named after the hill temple founded, by legend, by Lady Penh in 1372, the site at the confluence of the Mekong and Tonlé Sap became the Khmer capital after Angkor's abandonment and again under King Norodom in 1865.
summary.zh: 其名源于传说中奔夫人于1372年在山丘上建造的寺庙。此地位于湄公河与洞里萨河交汇处，吴哥被放弃后成为高棉都城，1865年诺罗敦国王再度定都于此。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Phnom Penh
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Phnom Penh

note: The 1372 founding and Ponhea Yat's capital dates are traditional.

summary.en: Yasovarman I founded Yasodharapura around 889, and for five centuries the Angkor region was the heart of the Khmer Empire. After 1431 the court moved south, though Angkor Wat remained a pilgrimage centre; Siam returned the province to French Cambodia in 1907.
summary.zh: 耶输跋摩一世约于889年建立耶输陀罗补罗，此后五个世纪里吴哥地区一直是高棉帝国的中心。1431年后王廷南迁，吴哥窟仍为朝圣之地；1907年暹罗将该省归还法属柬埔寨。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Angkor (Siem Reap)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Angkor
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Angkor

note: The capital moved between Angkor and nearby sites (e.g. Koh Ker, 928–944).

summary.en: Capital of the first Burmese empire, whose rulers and subjects built over 10,000 Buddhist temples and stupas on the plain beside the Irrawaddy between the 11th and 13th centuries; more than 2,000 survive.
summary.zh: 缅甸第一个帝国的都城。11至13世纪间，君主与臣民在伊洛瓦底江畔的平原上建造了一万多座佛寺与佛塔，现存两千余座。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Bagan
Michael Aung-Thwin, Pagan: The Origins of Modern Burma (University of Hawaii Press, 1985)
Wikipedia: Bagan
